old: As the letter A is the first of all letters, so the eternal God is first in the world
modern: The letter A is the foundation of all letters, and the primal God is the foundation of the world.

old: What Profit have those derived from learning, who worship not the good feet of Him who is possessed of pure knowledge ?
modern: What is the use of all the learning someone has acquired if they do not worship the good feet of the one who is pure knowledge?

old: They who are united to the glorious feet of Him who passes swiftly over the flower of the mind, shall flourish long above all worlds
modern: Someone who constantly thinks of the glorious feet of God, who is present in the flower-like mind, will live long on earth and in the heavenly worlds.

old: To those who meditate the feet of Him who is void of desire or aversion, evil shall never come
modern: Someone who meditates on the feet of a god who has no desire or aversion will never experience suffering.

old: The two-fold deeds that spring from darkness shall not adhere to those who delight in the true praise of God
modern: Those who love the true praise of God are not affected by the good and bad deeds that come from ignorance.

old: Those shall long proposer who abide in the faultless way of Him who has destroyed the five desires of the senses
modern: Those who follow the true path of the one who has destroyed the five desires that arise from the five senses will live long.

old: Anxiety of mind cannot be removed, except from those who are united to the feet of Him who is incomparable
modern: Anxiety cannot be relieved for those who are not united with the feet of the incomparable one.

old: None can swim the sea of vice, but those who are united to the feet of that gracious Being who is a sea of virtue
modern: Only those who hold the feet of the gracious one who is a sea of virtue can swim across the sea of vice.

old: The head that worships not the feet of Him who is possessed of eight attributes, is as useless as a sense without the power of sensation
modern: A head that does not bow to God, who has eight virtues, is as useless as a sense organ that cannot function.

old: None can swim the great sea of births but those who are united to the feet of God
modern: Only those who hold the feet of God can swim across the great sea of births.

old: By the continuance of rain the world is preserved in existence; it is therefore worthy to be called ambrosia
modern: The world continues to exist because of the unending rain, so rain is rightly called ambrosia.

old: Rain produces good food, and is itself food
modern: Rain produces good food, and it is itself food.

old: If the cloud, withholding rain, deceive (our hopes) hunger will long distress the sea-girt spacious world
modern: If the rain clouds fail to bring rain, hunger will torment and kill people in the vast world surrounded by the sea.

old: If the abundance of wealth imparting rain diminish, the labour of the plough must cease
modern: If the rain that brings wealth diminishes, the ploughman will not plough with his oxen.

old: Rain by its absence ruins men; and by its existence restores them to fortune
modern: Rain ruins people when it fails, and restores them to prosperity when it comes.

old: If no drop falls from the clouds, not even the green blade of grass will be seen
modern: If no drop of rain falls from the clouds, it is rare to see even the head of a green blade of grass.

old: Even the wealth of the wide sea will be diminished, if the cloud that has drawn (its waters) up gives them not back again (in rain)
modern: Even the wealth of the wide sea will shrink if the clouds that drew its water up do not give it back as rain.

old: If the heaven dry up, neither yearly festivals, nor daily worship will be offered in this world, to the celestials
modern: If the sky doesn't rain, then people on earth will not perform any festivals or daily worship for the gods.

old: If rain fall not, penance and alms-deeds will not dwell within this spacious world
modern: If the rain does not fall, the two virtues of giving to others and self-discipline will not exist in the world.

old: If it be said that the duties of life cannot be discharged by any person without water, so without rain there cannot be the flowing of water
modern: If there is no water, the world cannot exist, and without rain, there can be no order.

old: The end and aim of all treatise is to extol beyond all other excellence, the greatness of those who, while abiding in the rule of conduct peculiar to their state, have abandoned all desire
modern: The highest aim of every moral text is to praise the greatness of those who keep the conduct proper to their state and have given up all desire.

old: To describe the measure of the greatness of those who have forsaken the two-fold desires, is like counting the dead
modern: It is impossible to measure the greatness of those who have given up worldly desires, just as it is impossible to count all the people who have died in the world.

old: The greatness of those who have discovered the properties of both states of being, and renounced the world, shines forth on earth (beyond all others)
modern: The greatness of those who understand the nature of both life and death and practice virtue in this world is supreme.

old: He who guides his five senses by the hook of wisdom will be a seed in the world of heaven
modern: Someone who controls the five senses with the hook of wisdom will be a seed for the world of heaven.

old: Indra, the king of the inhabitants of the spacious heaven, is himself, a sufficient proof of the strength of him who has subdued his five senses
modern: Indra, the king of the heavens, is proof of the power of someone who has destroyed the five senses.

old: The great will do those things which is difficult to be done; but the mean cannot do them
modern: Great people do difficult things, while small people do easy things.

old: The world is within the knowledge of him who knows the properties of taste, sight, touch, hearing and smell
modern: The world is within the grasp of someone who understands the properties of taste, sight, touch, hearing and smell.

old: The hidden words of the men whose words are full of effect, will shew their greatness to the world
modern: The private words of people whose words always have effect will show their greatness to the world.

old: The anger of those who have ascended the mountain of goodness, though it continue but for a moment, cannot be resisted
modern: The anger of those who have climbed the mountain of goodness, even if it lasts only for a moment, is impossible to endure.

old: The virtuous are truly called Anthanar; because in their conduct towards all creatures they are clothed in kindness
modern: The virtuous are rightly called Anthanar, because they behave with kindness towards every living thing.

chapter: Assertion of the Strength of Virtue
old: Virtue will confer heaven and wealth; what greater source of happiness can man possess ?
modern: Virtue brings both honor and wealth, so what greater good can a living person obtain?

chapter: Assertion of the Strength of Virtue
old: There can be no greater source of good than (the practice of) virtue; there can be no greater source of evil than the forgetfulness of it
modern: There is no greater gain than virtue, and no greater loss than forgetting it.

chapter: Assertion of the Strength of Virtue
old: As much as possible, in every way, incessantly practise virtue
modern: Do as much good as you can, without stopping, everywhere you go.

chapter: Assertion of the Strength of Virtue
old: Let him who does virtuous deeds be of spotless mind; to that extent is virtue; all else is vain show
modern: True virtue is a mind that is free from blemish; everything else is just empty show.

chapter: Assertion of the Strength of Virtue
old: That conduct is virtue which is free from these four things, viz, malice, desire, anger and bitter speech
modern: Virtue is to avoid these four things: envy, desire, anger, and harsh speech.

chapter: Assertion of the Strength of Virtue
old: Defer not virtue to another day; receive her now; and at the dying hour she will be your undying friend
modern: Do good deeds right now without waiting for later, because they will be your undying companion when you die.

chapter: Assertion of the Strength of Virtue
old: The fruit of virtue need not be described in books; it may be inferred from seeing the bearer of a palanquin and the rider therein
modern: The benefit of virtue is self-evident when you see the palanquin bearer and the rider.

chapter: Assertion of the Strength of Virtue
old: If one allows no day to pass without some good being done, his conduct will be a stone to block up the passage to other births
modern: If a person does not let a single day go by without doing good deeds, those good deeds will act as a stone that blocks the path to future rebirths.

chapter: Assertion of the Strength of Virtue
old: Only that pleasure which flows from domestic virtue is pleasure; all else is not pleasure, and it is without praise
modern: True pleasure and praise come only from virtuous actions; everything else is ultimately painful and brings no glory.

chapter: Assertion of the Strength of Virtue
old: That is virtue which each ought to do, and that is vice which each should shun
modern: Virtue is what a person should do, and vice is what a person should avoid.

old: He will be called a (true) householder, who is a firm support to the virtuous of the three orders in
modern: Someone is called a true householder when they are a firm support to the virtuous of the other three orders.

old: He will be said to flourish in domestic virtue who aids the forsaken, the poor, and the dead
modern: Someone flourishes in household virtue when they help the abandoned, the poor, and the dead.

old: The chief (duty of the householder) is to preserve the five-fold rule (of conduct) towards the manes, the Gods, his guests, his relations and himself
modern: The chief duty of a householder is to care properly for the ancestors, the gods, guests, relatives, and oneself.

old: His descendants shall never fail who, living in the domestic state, fears vice (in the acquisition of property) and shares his food (with others)
modern: Someone who avoids sinful ways of earning wealth and shares their food with others will never lose their prosperity or lineage.

old: If the married life possess love and virtue, these will be both its duty and reward
modern: If a household has love and virtue, these are its character and its benefit.

old: What will he who lives virtuously in the domestic state gain by going into the other, (ascetic) state ?
modern: If someone lives a virtuous life in a family, what benefit can they gain by becoming a monk?

old: Among all those who labour (for future happiness) he is greatest who lives well in the household state
modern: Among those who strive for happiness, the one who lives a domestic life according to its nature is the greatest.

old: The householder who, not swerving from virtue, helps the ascetic in his way, endures more than those who endure penance
modern: A life of virtue that guides others and never strays is stronger than the endurance of ascetics.

old: The marriage state is truly called virtue The other state is also good, if others do not reproach it
modern: A virtuous home life is praised as true virtue, and a monastic life is also good if it is not blamed by others.

old: He who on earth has lived in the conjugal state as he should live, will be placed among the Gods who dwell in heaven
modern: Someone who lives a virtuous married life on earth will be honored among the gods in heaven.

old: She who has the excellence of home virtues, and can expend within the means of her husband, is a help in the domestic state
modern: A woman who has the virtues of a good home and who spends within her husband's means is a help in domestic life.

old: If the wife be devoid of domestic excellence, whatever (other) greatness be possessed, the conjugal state, is nothing
modern: If a wife lacks the virtues of a good home, then whatever other greatness a man has, married life is worth nothing.

old: If his wife be eminent (in virtue), what does (that man) not possess ? If she be without excellence, what does (he) possess ?
modern: If a man's wife is excellent, what does he not have? If she lacks excellence, what does he have?

old: What is more excellent than a wife, if she possess the stability of chastity ?
modern: What is more valuable than a woman who has the firmness of chastity?

old: If she, who does not worship God, but who rising worships her husband, say, "let it rain," it will rain
modern: If a woman who worships no god but rises and serves her husband says "let it rain", it will rain.

old: She is a wife who unweariedly guards herself, takes care of her husband, and preserves an unsullied fame
modern: A good wife protects her own character, takes care of her husband, and maintains their shared good reputation without ever getting tired or losing her resolve.

old: What avails the guard of a prison ? The chief guard of a woman is her chastity
modern: What use is the guard of a prison? A woman's own chastity is her surest guard.

old: If women shew reverence to their husbands, they will obtain great excellence in the world where the gods flourish
modern: Women who show reverence to their husbands will gain great honour in the world where the gods live.

old: The man whose wife seeks not the praise (of chastity) cannot walk with lion-like stately step, before those who revile them
modern: A man whose wife does not seek praise cannot walk with a proud, lion-like gait before those who revile him.

old: The excellence of a wife is the good of her husband; and good children are the jewels of that goodness
modern: A virtuous wife is the true blessing of a home, and having good children is the beautiful ornament that enhances that blessing.

old: Among all the benefits that may be acquired, we know no greater benefit than the acquisition of intelligent children
modern: Among all the gains a person can get, there is no greater gain than having wise and virtuous children.

old: The evils of the seven births shall not touch those who abtain children of a good disposition, free from vice
modern: If you have children with good character who are free from blame, no evils or sorrows will touch them across all seven births.

old: Men will call their sons their wealth, because it flows to them through the deeds which they (sons) perform on their behalf
modern: People call their children their wealth, and that wealth comes from the children's actions.

old: The rice in which the little hand of their children has dabbled will be far sweeter (to the parent) than ambrosia
modern: Food that a child has touched with their small hands is sweeter to a parent than nectar.

old: The touch of children gives pleasure to the body, and the hearing of their words, pleasure to the ear
modern: The touch of children brings pleasure to the body, and hearing their words brings pleasure to the ear.

old: "The pipe is sweet, the lute is sweet," say those who have not heard the prattle of their own children
modern: People who have never heard their own children's babbling are the ones who say the flute and lute are sweet.

old: The benefit which a father should confer on his son is to give him precedence in the assembly of the learned
modern: A father's greatest benefit to his son is to make him learned so he can take the highest seat in an assembly of wise people.

old: That their children should possess knowledge is more pleasing to all men of this great earth than to themselves
modern: It pleases everyone on this wide earth more to see their children gain knowledge than to gain it themselves.

old: The mother who hears her son called "a wise man" will rejoice more than she did at his birth
modern: A mother feels greater joy when she hears her son praised as wise than she did when she gave birth to him.

old: (So to act) that it may be said "by what great penance did his father beget him," is the benefit which a son should render to his father
modern: A son's true service to his father is to make people say, "What great penance did the father perform to beget such a son?

old: Is there any fastening that can shut in love ? Tears of the affectionate will publish the love that is within
modern: There is no lock that can keep true love hidden, because a single teardrop from a loving person will reveal it.

old: Those who are destitute of love appropriate all they have to themselves; but those who possess love consider even their bones to belong to others
modern: Those without love consider everything their own, while those with love consider even their own bones to belong to others.

old: They say that the union of soul and body in man is the fruit of the union of love and virtue (in a former birth)
modern: The continuous connection between the body and the precious soul is the reward for the good deeds and love accumulated in a past life.

old: Love begets desire: and that (desire) begets the immeasureable excellence of friendship
modern: Love creates a deep desire to connect with others, and that desire brings about the boundless excellence of true friendship.

old: The touch of children gives pleasure to the body, and the hearing of their words, pleasure to the ear.
modern: The touch of children gives pleasure to the body, and hearing them speak gives pleasure to the ear.

old: The ignorant say that love is an ally to virtue only, but it is also a help to get out of vice
modern: The ignorant say love supports virtue only, but it also helps a person escape wrongdoing.

old: Virtue will burn up the soul which is without love, even as the sun burns up the creature which is without bone, ie worms
modern: Virtue will burn the soul that lacks love, just as the sun burns the boneless worm.

old: The domestic state of that man whose mind is without love is like the flourishing of a withered tree upon the parched desert
modern: A life without love is like a withered tree sprouting in a desert.

old: Of what avail are all the external members (of the body) to those who are destitute of love, the internal member
modern: What use are all the outer parts of the body to someone who lacks love, which is the inner part?

old: That body alone which is inspired with love contains a living soul: if void of it, (the body) is bone overlaid with skin
modern: A body is alive only when it is guided by love; without love, it is just skin covering bone.

old: The whole design of living in the domestic state and laying up (property) is (to be able) to exercise the benevolence of hospitality
modern: The purpose of earning and protecting wealth at home is to be able to host guests and help them.

old: It is not fit that one should wish his guests to be outside (his house) even though he were eating the food of immortality
modern: Even if you are eating food that prevents death, it is not good to eat alone while keeping guests outside.

old: The domestic life of the man that daily entertains the guests who come to him shall not be laid waste by poverty
modern: A person who consistently hosts guests every day will not suffer from poverty or have their life ruined.

old: Lakshmi with joyous mind shall dwell in the house of that man who, with cheerful countenance, entertains the good as guests
modern: The goddess of wealth will happily reside in the home of someone who welcomes worthy guests with a cheerful, smiling face.

old: Is it necessary to sow the field of the man who, having feasted his guests, eats what may remain ?
modern: Is there any need to sow the field of the man who eats only what is left after feeding his guests?

old: He who, having entertained the guests that have come, looks out for others who may yet come, will be a welcome guest to the inhabitants of heaven
modern: Someone who takes care of a guest who has arrived and also looks forward to the next guest to come will be a welcome guest for the inhabitants of heaven in the afterlife.

old: The advantages of benevolence cannot be measured; the measure (of the virtue) of the guests (entertained) is the only measure
modern: The benefit of entertaining guests cannot be measured by any standard, as the value of the hospitality is determined solely by the worthiness of the guests themselves.

old: Those who have taken no part in the benevolence of hospitality shall (at length lament) saying, "we have laboured and laid up wealth and are now without support."
modern: Those who took no part in the kindness of hospitality will lament that they laboured and stored up wealth and now have no support.

old: That stupidity which excercises no hospitality is poverty in the midst of wealth It is the property of the stupid
modern: The stupidity that offers no hospitality is poverty in the middle of wealth, and it belongs to the foolish.

old: As the Anicham flower fades in smelling, so fades the guest when the face is turned away
modern: Just as the anicham flower withers when it is smelled, a guest withers when the host turns their face away.

old: Sweet words are those which imbued with love and free from deceit flow from the mouth of the virtuous
modern: Sweet words are spoken by people who know the truth, and they are full of love and free from deceit.

old: Sweet speech, with a cheerful countenance is better than a gift made with a joyous mind
modern: A smiling face and kind words are better than giving a gift with a happy heart.

old: Sweet speech, flowing from the heart (uttered) with a cheerful countenance and a sweet look, is true virtue
modern: True virtue is speaking sweet words from the heart with a pleasant look and a smiling face.

old: Sorrow-increasing poverty shall not come upon those who use towards all, pleasure-increasing sweetness of speech
modern: Those who speak sweet words that bring pleasure to everyone will not experience the sorrow of poverty.

old: Humility and sweetness of speech are the ornaments of man; all others are not (ornaments)
modern: Humility and speaking sweet words are the only true ornaments for a person; all other adornments are not.

old: If a man, while seeking to speak usefully, speaks also sweetly, his sins will diminish and his virtue increase
modern: If someone seeks out good and speaks sweet words that benefit others, their sins will diminish and their virtue will grow.

old: That speech which, while imparting benefits ceases not to please, will yield righteousness (for this world) and merit (for the next world)
modern: Words that give a beneficial advantage to others and never depart from good character bring happiness and goodness to the speaker, and yield righteousness for this world and merit for the next.

old: Sweet speech, free from harm to others, will give pleasure both in this world and in the next
modern: Sweet words that are free from meanness and do not cause pain to others will bring happiness in this world and in the next.

old: Why does he use harsh words, who sees the pleasure which sweet speech yields ?
modern: If someone knows that sweet words bring happiness, what is the use of using harsh words?

old: To say disagreeable things when agreeable are at hand is like eating unripe fruit when there is ripe
modern: Speaking harsh words when sweet ones are available is like eating unripe fruit when ripe fruit is present.

old: (The gift of) heaven and earth is not an equivalent for a benefit which is conferred where none had been received
modern: If someone helps you even when you have never helped them before, the earth and the heavens combined cannot repay that favor.

old: A favour conferred in the time of need, though it be small (in itself), is (in value) much larger than the world
modern: A small favor done at the right time is more valuable than the entire world.

old: If we weigh the excellence of a benefit which is conferred without weighing the return, it is larger than the sea
modern: Helping someone without expecting a reward is a benefit that is greater than the sea.

old: Though the benefit conferred be as small as a millet seed, those who know its advantage will consider it as large as a palmyra fruit
modern: If someone gives a small help as tiny as a millet seed, those who know its benefit will consider it as large as a palm tree.

old: The benefit itself is not the measure of the benefit; the worth of those who have received it is its measure
modern: The size of a kindness is not the measure of it; the worth of the person who received it is the measure.

old: Forsake not the friendship of those who have been your staff in adversity Forget not be benevolence of the blameless
modern: You should never forget the friendship of people with a pure character, and you should not abandon the friends who supported you during times of trouble.

old: (The wise) will remember throughout their seven-fold births the love of those who have wiped away their affliction
modern: Good people will remember the friendship of those who wiped away their suffering through all seven of their births.

old: It is not good to forget a benefit; it is good to forget an injury even in the very moment (in which it is inflicted)
modern: It is not good to forget a good deed done by someone, but it is good to forget a bad deed done by them on that very day.

old: Though one inflict an injury great as murder, it will perish before the thought of one benefit (formerly) conferred
modern: Even if someone who previously helped you later commits a deadly harm like murder, remembering just one good deed they did for you will erase all that harm.

old: He who has killed every virtue may yet escape; there is no escape for him who has killed a benefit
modern: Someone who has destroyed great virtues may still find a way to escape, but there is no escape for someone who has destroyed a benefit.

old: That equity which consists in acting with equal regard to each of (the three) divisions of men enemies, strangers and friends is a pre-eminent virtue
modern: Justice that treats enemies, strangers and friends with equal regard is the greatest virtue.

old: The wealth of the man of rectitude will not perish, but will bring happiness also to his posterity
modern: The wealth of a just person does not perish and will protect their descendants.

old: Forsake in the very moment (of acquisition) that gain which, though it should bring advantage, is without equity
modern: Even if unjust gains bring benefits, abandon them immediately.

old: The worthy and unworthy may be known by the existence or otherwise of good offsprings
modern: The worthy and the unworthy can be told apart by whether or not they have good children.

old: Loss and gain come not without cause; it is the ornament of the wise to preserve evenness of mind (under both)
modern: Loss and gain happen for a reason, and it is the wise person's ornament to remain even-minded in both situations.

old: Let him whose mind departing from equity commits sin well consider thus within himself, "I shall perish."
modern: If a person abandons justice and decides to do wrong, they should know that they are heading toward ruin.

old: The great will not regard as poverty the low estate of that man who dwells in the virtue of equity
modern: The great will not count it as poverty when someone who lives by justice falls into low estate.

old: To incline to neither side, but to rest impartial as the even-fixed scale is the ornament of the wise
modern: A wise person's beauty is their ability to remain perfectly impartial, like a balance scale that weighs things fairly without leaning to either side.

old: Freedom from obliquity of speech is rectitude, if there be (corresponding) freedom from bias of mind
modern: True justice is being completely unbiased in your mind and speaking without any crookedness.

old: The true merchandize of merchants is to guard and do by the things of others as they do by their own
modern: A trader who treats others' property as his own will have a successful trade.

old: Self-control will place (a man) among the Gods; the want of it will drive (him) into the thickest darkness (of hell)
modern: Self-control elevates a person to the realm of the gods, while a lack of self-control leads them into the deepest darkness.

old: Let self-control be guarded as a treasure; there is no greater source of good for man than that
modern: Guard self-control as a treasure, because there is no greater gain for a living being than that.

old: Knowing that self-control is knowledge, if a man should control himself, in the prescribed course, such self-control will bring him distinction among the wise
modern: Knowing that controlling oneself is true wisdom, if a person lives a disciplined life, their self-control will be recognized by good people and bring them great distinction.

old: More lofty than a mountain will be the greatness of that man who without swerving from his domestic state, controls himself
modern: A person who remains firm in their station and controls themselves will be greater than a mountain.

old: Humility is good in all; but especially in the rich it is (the excellence of) higher riches
modern: Humility is good for everyone, but for the wealthy, it is like having another special kind of wealth.

old: Should one throughout a single birth, like a tortoise keep in his five senses, the fruit of it will prove a safe-guard to him throughout the seven-fold births.
modern: If someone draws in the five senses like a tortoise for a single birth, it will protect them through seven births.

old: Whatever besides you leave unguarded, guard your tongue; otherwise errors of speech and the consequent misery will ensue
modern: Even if you fail to guard everything else, you should at least guard your tongue, because failing to do so will lead to the misery of making a mistake with your words.

old: If a man's speech be productive of a single evil, all the good by him will be turned into evil
modern: If a person speaks even one evil word that causes harm to others, all the good they have done will be turned into evil.

old: The wound which has been burnt in by fire may heal, but a wound burnt in by the tongue will never heal
modern: A wound from fire can heal, but a wound from the tongue never does.

old: Virtue, seeking for an opportunity, will come into the path of that man who, possessed of learning and self-control, guards himself against anger
modern: Virtue waits for the right time to approach the path of a learned person who has mastered their anger and remains self-controlled.

old: Propriety of conduct leads to eminence, it should therefore be preserved more carefully than life
modern: Good conduct brings greatness to everyone, so it should be protected more carefully than life itself.

old: Let propriety of conduct be laboriously preserved and guarded; though one know and practise and excel in many virtues, that will be an eminent aid
modern: Guard good conduct with effort and care, because even for someone who knows and practises many virtues it is the greatest help.

old: Propriety of conduct is true greatness of birth, and impropriety will sink into a mean birth
modern: Good conduct is the true sign of a noble family, and bad conduct makes someone seem like they were born into a low family.

old: A Brahman though he should forget the Vedas may recover it by reading; but, if he fail in propriety of conduct even his high birth will be destroyed
modern: A person can regain forgotten knowledge by studying, but if they lose their good conduct, their high birth is destroyed.

old: Just as the envious man will be without wealth, so will the man of destitute of propriety of conduct be without greatness
modern: Just as the envious person has no wealth, the person without good conduct has no greatness.

old: Those firm in mind will not slacken in their observance of the proprieties of life, knowing, as they do, the misery that flows from the transgression from them
modern: Those who are firm in mind never slacken in good conduct, because they know the misery that comes from breaking it.

old: From propriety of conduct men obtain greatness; from impropriety comes insufferable disgrace
modern: Good conduct brings people greatness, while bad conduct brings them undeserved disgrace.

old: Propriety of conduct is the seed of virtue; impropriety will ever cause sorrow
modern: Good conduct is the seed of blessings, while bad conduct always brings sorrow.

old: Those who study propriety of conduct will not speak evil, even forgetfully
modern: People with good character will not speak harmful words, even by accident.

old: Those who know not how to act agreeably to the world, though they have learnt many things, are still ignorant
modern: Someone who has read many books but does not know how to live in harmony with the world and act according to the ways of good people is still ignorant.

old: The folly of desiring her who is the property of another will not be found in those who know (the attributes of) virtue and (the rights of) property
modern: The foolishness of lusting after someone else's wife does not exist in people who have studied and understood virtue and wealth.

old: Among all those who stand on the outside of virtue, there are no greater fools than those who stand outside their neighbour's door
modern: Among all people who abandon virtue, there are no bigger fools than those who stand outside their neighbor's door lusting after his wife.

old: Certainly they are no better than dead men who desire evil towards the wife of those who
modern: Someone who schemes to do evil to the wife of a person who trusts them is no different from a dead person.

old: However great one may be, what does it avail if, without at all considering his guilt, he goes unto the wife of another ?
modern: No matter how great someone is, they lose all their greatness if they enter another person's wife without even thinking about their own guilt.

old: He who thinks lightly of going into the wife of another acquires guilt that will abide with him imperishably and for ever
modern: Someone who thinks it is easy to sleep with another man's wife and does so will acquire a permanent, undying stigma.

old: Hatred, sin, fear, disgrace; these four will never leave him who goes in to his neighbour's wife
modern: Someone who goes to another man's wife will never be rid of hatred, sin, fear, and disgrace.

old: He who desires not the womanhood of her who should walk according to the will of another will be praised as a virtuous house-holder
modern: A man who does not desire another man's wife is a righteous householder.

old: That noble manliness which looks not at the wife of another is the virtue and dignity of the great
modern: The manliness that does not look at another man's wife is the virtue and dignity of the great.

old: Is it asked, "who are those who shall obtain good in this world surrounded by the terror-producing sea ?" Those who touch not the shoulder of her who belongs to another
modern: In a world surrounded by the terrifying ocean, the people who are worthy of good things are those who do not touch the shoulder of someone who belongs to another.

old: Though a man perform no virtuous deeds and commit (every) vice, it will be well if he desire not the womanhood of her who is within the limit (of the house) of another
modern: Even if a person does not follow virtue and commits many sins, it is good if they do not desire another man's wife.

old: To bear with those who revile us, just as the earth bears up those who dig it, is the first of virtues
modern: Bearing with those who revile you is the highest virtue, just as the earth bears up those who dig it.

old: Bear with reproach even when you can retaliate; but to forget it will be still better than that
modern: It is good to always bear the harm done by others, but it is even better to forget it completely.

old: To neglect hospitality is poverty of poverty To bear with the ignorant is might of might
modern: The worst form of poverty is turning away a guest without feeding them, and the greatest form of strength is tolerating the actions of ignorant fools.

old: If you desire that greatness should never leave, you preserve in your conduct the exercise of patience
modern: If you want your greatness never to leave you, keep patience in your conduct.

old: (The wise) will not at all esteem the resentful They will esteem the patient just as the gold which they lay up with care
modern: People will not value someone who seeks revenge, but they will treasure someone who patiently endures hardship as if it were gold.

old: The pleasure of the resentful continues for a day The praise of the patient will continue until (the final destruction of) the world
modern: The pleasure of someone who seeks revenge lasts only one day, while the praise of someone who is patient lasts until the world ends.

old: Though others inflict injuries on you, yet compassionating the evil (that will come upon them) it will be well not to do them anything contrary to virtue
modern: Even when others injure you, it is right to pity the evil that will come to them and to do nothing against virtue in return.

old: Let a man by patience overcome those who through pride commit excesses
modern: One should overcome those who commit wrongs through pride by using one's own patience.

old: Those who bear with the uncourteous speech of the insolent are as pure as the ascetics
modern: Those who patiently endure the harsh words of those who act without limits are as pure as ascetics.

old: Those who endure abstinence from food are great, next to those who endure the uncourteous speech of others
modern: Those who endure fasting are considered great, but those who endure harsh words from others are considered even greater.

old: Let a man esteem that disposition which is free from envy in the same manner as propriety of conduct
modern: Let a person value a mind free of envy as highly as good conduct itself.

old: Amongst all attainable excellences there is none equal to that of being free from envy towords others
modern: Among all the excellences a person can reach, none equals being free of envy towards others.

old: Of him who instead of rejoicing in the wealth of others, envies it, it will be said "he neither desires virtue not wealth."
modern: Someone who envies others' good fortune is said to not desire virtue or wealth for themselves.

old: (The wise) knowing the misery that comes from transgression will not through envy commit unrighteous deeds
modern: Wise people do not commit unrighteous acts through envy because they know that such evil paths bring misery.

old: To those who cherish envy that is enough Though free from enemies that (envy) will bring destruction
modern: Someone who has envy does not need an enemy to destroy them, because their own envy is enough to cause their ruin.

old: He who is envious at a gift (made to another) will with his relations utterly perish destitute of food and rainment
modern: Someone who envies a gift made to another will perish with their relatives, without food or clothing.

old: Lakshmi envying (the prosperity) of the envious man will depart and introduce him to her sister
modern: Lakshmi, who brings wealth, will see a person who is envious of the prosperity of others, point him out to her older sister who brings poverty, and leave him.

old: Envy will destroy (a man's) wealth (in his world) and drive him into the pit of fire (in the world to come.)
modern: Envy is an unmatched evil that destroys a person's wealth in this world and leads them into the fire of hell in the next.

old: The wealth of a man of envious mind and the poverty of the righteous will be pondered
modern: People are surprised and deeply ponder why the life of someone with an envious heart flourishes while the life of a blameless person suffers.

old: Never have the envious become great; never have those who are free from envy been without greatness
modern: No one who is envious becomes great, and no one who is free from envy fails to achieve greatness.

old: If a man departing from equity covet the property (of others), at that very time will his family be destroyed and guilt be incurred
modern: If someone covets another person's honest wealth without fairness, their family will be destroyed and they will incur guilt.

old: Those who blush at the want of equity will not commit disgraceful acts through desire of the profit that may be gained
modern: Someone who is ashamed of injustice will not commit shameful acts for the sake of gain.

old: Those who desire the higher pleasures (of heaven) will not act unjustly through desire of the trifling joy. (in this life.)
modern: Someone who desires the lasting happiness that comes from righteousness will not commit wrongful acts for the sake of fleeting, small pleasures.

old: The wise who have conquered their senses and are free from crime, will not covet (the things of others), with the thought "we are destitute."
modern: People who have conquered their senses and are free from crime will not covet other people's wealth, even if they are experiencing poverty.

old: What is the advantage of extensive and accurate knowledge if a man through covetousness act senselessly towards all ?
modern: What is the use of vast knowledge if a person, driven by greed, acts foolishly towards everyone?

old: If he, who through desire of the virtue of kindness abides in the domestic state ie, the path in which it may be obtained, covet (the property of others) and think of evil methods (to obtain it), he will perish
modern: Someone who seeks grace and follows the righteous path will be destroyed if they desire wealth and think of evil deeds.

old: Desire not the gain of covetousness In the enjoyment of its fruits there is no glory
modern: You should avoid the wealth gained by coveting other people's property, because the benefits of that wealth are not good when you actually enjoy them.

old: If it is weighed, "what is the indestructibility of wealth," it is freedom from covetousness
modern: The way to keep wealth from decreasing is to not desire what belongs to someone else.

old: Lakshmi, knowing the manner (in which she may approach) will immediately come to those wise men who, knowing that it is virtue, covet not the property of others
modern: Fortune comes readily to wise people who know it is virtuous not to covet what belongs to others.

old: To covet (the wealth of another) regardless of consequences will bring destruction That greatness (of mind) which covets not will give victory
modern: Coveting another person's wealth without thinking of the consequences will bring destruction, but greatness of mind that does not desire that wealth will bring victory.

old: Though one do not even speak of virtue and live in sin, it will be well if it be said of him "he does not backbite."
modern: Even if someone does not talk about virtue and commits sins, it is good if people say that they do not backbite others.

old: To smile deceitfully (in another's presence) after having reviled him to his destruction (behind his back) is a greater evil than the commission of (every other) sin and the destruction of (every) virtue
modern: Pretending to be friendly and smiling at someone to their face while secretly speaking evil about them behind their back is worse than openly rejecting virtue and committing sins.

old: Death rather than life will confer upon the deceitful backbiter the profit which (the treatises on) virtue point out
modern: Moral texts say that death rather than life brings profit to someone who slanders others behind their back.

old: Though you speak without kindness before another's face speak not in his absence words which regard not the evil subsequently resulting from it
modern: It is acceptable to speak harshly to someone's face, but you should not speak ill of them behind their back without considering the negative consequences.

old: The emptiness of that man's mind who (merely) praises virtue will be seen from the meanness of reviling another behind his back
modern: The emptiness of someone who merely praises virtue shows itself in the meanness of speaking against another behind their back.

old: The character of the faults of that man who publishes abroad the faults of others will be sought out and published
modern: Someone who points out the faults of others will have their own faults, especially the most severe ones, discovered and exposed by others.

old: Those who know not to live in friendship with amusing conversation will by back-biting estrange even their relatives
modern: Those who do not know how to make friends with pleasant words will, by speaking ill of others, cause even their friends to leave them.

old: What will those not do to strangers whose nature leads them to publish abroad the faults of their intimate friends ?
modern: Someone who habitually speaks ill of their close friends will surely do the same to strangers.

old: The world through charity supports the weight of those who reproach others observing their absence
modern: The earth tolerates the physical burden of people who speak bad words about others behind their backs, as if bearing their weight is a righteous duty.

old: If they observed their own faults as they observe the faults of others, would any evil happen to men ?
modern: If people observed their own faults as closely as they observe the faults of others, no harm would come to them.

old: He who to the disgust of many speaks useless things will be despised by all
modern: Someone who speaks useless words that many people hate will be despised by everyone.

old: To speak useless things in the presence of many is a greater evil than to do unkind things towards friends
modern: Speaking useless words in front of many people is worse than doing unkind things to friends.

old: That conversation in which a man utters forth useless things will say of him "he is without virtue."
modern: When someone speaks at length about useless things, their words announce that they lack virtue and righteousness.

old: The words devoid of profit or pleasure which a man speaks will, being inconsistent with virtue,
modern: Speaking useless and unrefined words to a crowd will remove someone from goodness and virtue, and will not bring them any profit or pleasure.

old: If the good speak vain words their eminence and excellence will leave them
modern: When people of good character speak useless words, their glory and excellence will immediately leave them.

old: Call not him a man who parades forth his empty words Call him the chaff of men
modern: Do not call someone who parades empty words a person; call them the chaff among people.

old: Let the wise if they will, speak things without excellence; it will be well for them not to speak useless things
modern: Wise people might speak harsh or unjust words, but it is better for them to avoid speaking useless words.

old: The wise who seek after rare pleasures will not speak words that have not much weight in them
modern: The wise who seek rare benefits will not speak words that lack great benefit.

old: Those wise men who are without faults and are freed from ignorance will not even forgetfully speak things that profit not
modern: People with pure, clear knowledge who are free from ignorance will never even by mistake speak useless words.

old: Speak what is useful, and speak not useless words
modern: Speak words that are useful, and do not speak useless words.

old: Those who have experience of evil deeds will not fear, but the excellent will fear the pride of sin
modern: Those who are used to doing evil deeds do not fear the pride of sin, but noble people do.

old: Because evil produces evil, therefore should evil be feared more than fire
modern: Since evil produces more evil, it should be feared more than fire.

old: To do no evil to enemies will be called the chief of all virtues.
modern: The highest wisdom is to not do harm to those who hate you.

old: Even though forgetfulness meditate not the ruin of another Virtue will meditate the ruin of him who thus meditates
modern: Even if you forget, you should not plot the ruin of another person, because virtue will surround and plot the ruin of anyone who does.

old: Commit not evil, saying, "I am poor": if you do, you will become poorer still
modern: Do not commit evil deeds just because you are poor, because doing so will only make you poorer still.

old: Let him not do evil to others who desires not that sorrows should pursue him
modern: Someone who does not want to suffer should not do harmful things to others.

old: However great be the enmity men have incurred they may still live The enmity of sin will incessantly pursue and kill
modern: Even if someone escapes every other enemy they have, the enmity of sin will relentlessly follow them and destroy them.

old: Destruction will dwell at the heels of those who commit evil even as their shadow that leaves them not
modern: Destruction follows those who do evil, just as their shadow never leaves their feet.

old: If a man love himself, let him not commit any sin however small
modern: If someone loves themselves, they should avoid committing even the smallest evil act against others.

old: Know ye that he is freed from destruction who commits no evil, going to neither side of the right path
modern: A person who does not stray from the right path to commit evil deeds is free from harm and destruction.

old: Benevolence seeks not a return. What does the world give back to the clouds ?
modern: Doing good asks for no return, just as the world gives nothing back to the clouds.

old: All the wealth acquired with perseverance by the worthy is for the exercise of benevolence
modern: Wealth earned through hard work is meant to be used for helping those who are worthy or in need.

old: It is difficult to obtain another good equal to benevolence either in this world or in that of the gods
modern: It is difficult to find a good deed equal to benevolence in the world of the gods and in this world.

old: He truly lives who knows (and discharges) the proper duties (of benevolence) He who knows them not will be reckoned among the dead
modern: Someone who knows how to help others truly lives, while someone who doesn't is considered as good as dead.

old: The wealth of that man of eminent knowledge who desires to exercise the benevolence approved of by the world, is like the full waters of a city-tank
modern: The wealth of a person of great knowledge who wants to do good for others is like a town's tank filled with water.

old: The wealth of a man (possessed of the virtue) of benevolence is like the ripening of a fruitful tree in the midst of a town
modern: Wealth that is possessed by someone who is benevolent is like a fruitful tree in the middle of a town that has ripened with fruit.

old: If wealth be in the possession of a man who has the great excellence (of benevolence), it is like a tree which as a medicine is an infallible cure for disease
modern: If wealth is possessed by someone with a great and benevolent heart, it is like a tree that provides a cure for all illnesses, where every part of it can be used as medicine.

old: The wise who know what is duty will not scant their benevolence even when they are without wealth
modern: Wise people who know their duty do not cut back on doing good, even when they are without wealth.

old: The poverty of a benevolent man, is nothing but his inability to exercise the same
modern: The poverty of a good person is their inability to help others, which makes them grieve because they cannot do the good deeds they want to do.

old: If it be said that loss will result from benevolence, such loss is worth being procured even by the sale of one's self
modern: If a loss comes from doing good, that loss is worth buying even by selling yourself.

old: To give to the destitute is true charity All other gifts have the nature of (what is done for) a measured return
modern: True charity is giving to the poor, while all other gifts are given with the expectation of a return.

old: To beg is evil, even though it were said that it is a good path (to heaven) To give is good, even though it were said that those who do so cannot obtain heaven
modern: It is wrong to beg even if people say it is a good path, and it is good to give even if people say it does not lead to heaven.

old: (Even in a low state) not to adopt the mean expedient of saying "I have nothing," but to give, is the characteristic of the mad of noble birth
modern: Giving instead of taking the mean way out by saying "I have nothing" is the mark of a person of noble birth.

old: To see men begging from us in disagreeable, until we see their pleasant countenance
modern: It is painful to see someone begging until you see their happy face after they have received what they asked for.

old: The power of those who perform penance is the power of enduring hunger It is inferior to the power of those who remove the hunger (of others)
modern: The strength of enduring one's own hunger is inferior to the strength of those who relieve the hunger of others.

old: The removal of the killing hunger of the poor is the place for one to lay up his wealth
modern: Relieving the starving poor of their hunger is the place where a person who gains wealth can safely store it for future use.

old: The fiery disease of hunger shall never touch him who habitually distributes his food to others
modern: A person who habitually shares their food with others will not be afflicted by the terrible disease of hunger.

old: Do the hard-eyed who lay up and lose their possessions not know the happiness which springs from the pleasure of giving ?
modern: Heartless people who hoard their wealth and eventually lose it do not know the joy of giving and seeing others happy.

old: Solitary and unshared eating for the sake of filling up one's own riches is certainly much more
modern: Eating alone to fill one's own wealth is worse than begging.

old: Nothing is more unpleasant than death: yet even that is pleasant where charity cannot be exercised
modern: Nothing is more painful than death, but it is even more painful to be unable to give to the poor.

old: Give to the poor and live with praise There is no greater profit to man than that
modern: Live a life of generous giving to the poor so that you gain great fame, because there is no greater reward for human life than that.

old: Whatsoever is spoken in the world will abide as praise upon that man who gives alms to the poor
modern: The praise of someone who gives alms to the poor is what everyone will speak about.

old: There is nothing that stands forth in the world imperishable, except fame, exalted in solitary greatness
modern: Nothing else in the world lasts forever except for exalted fame that has no equal.

old: If one has acquired extensive fame within the limits of this earth, the world of the Gods will no longer praise those sages who have attained that world
modern: When someone wins wide fame within this earth, the world of the gods stops praising the sages who have reached it.

old: Prosperity to the body of fame, resulting in poverty to the body of flesh and the stability to the former arising from the death of the latter, are achievable only by the wise
modern: Gaining wealth from poverty and gaining lasting fame from death are difficult to achieve for anyone other than the wise.

old: If you are born (in this world), be born with qualities conductive to fame From those who are destitute of them it will be better not to be born
modern: If you are born, be born with qualities that bring fame; for those who lack them it is better not to be born.

old: Why do those who cannot live with praise, grieve those who despise them, instead of grieving themselves for their own inability
modern: Why should someone who cannot live with fame be upset at those who despise them, instead of being upset with themselves for their own shortcomings?

old: Not to beget fame will be esteemed a disgrace by the wise in this world
modern: If you do not leave behind a legacy of fame, people will call your life a disgrace.

old: The ground which supports a body without fame will diminish in its rich produce
modern: The land that supports a body without fame will diminish in its rich produce.

old: Those live who live without disgrace Those who live without fame live not
modern: Someone who lives without blame is truly living, while someone who lives without fame is not truly living.

old: The wealth of kindness is wealth of wealth, in as much as the wealth of property is possessed by the basest of men
modern: The wealth of kindness is the greatest wealth, as even the lowest people possess material wealth.

old: (Stand) in the good path, consider, and be kind. Even considering according to the conflicting tenets of the different sects, kindness will be your best aid, (in the acquisition of heavenly bliss.)
modern: Seek the good path and be compassionate, because even after exploring many different systems, compassion alone will be your aid.

old: They will never enter the world of darkness and wretchedness whose minds are the abode of kindness
modern: People with merciful hearts do not enter the dark world of misery and hell.

old: (The wise) say that the evils, which his soul would dread, will never come upon the man who exercises kindness and protects the life (of other creatures)
modern: A person who protects all living beings and shows them mercy will not have to fear any harm coming to their own soul.

old: This great rich earth over which the wind blows, is a witness that sorrow never comes upon the kindhearted
modern: People who are kind and merciful do not experience sorrow, and the vast, prosperous earth where the winds blow is a witness to this.

old: (The wise) say that those who neglect kindness and practise cruelties, neglected virtue (in their former birth), and forgot (the sorrows which they must suffer.)
modern: Those who abandon kindness and commit cruel acts are said to have lost their wealth and forgotten the suffering they will endure.

old: As this world is not for those who are without wealth, so that world is not for those who are without kindness
modern: Just as this world is not for those without wealth, that world is not for those without kindness.

old: Those who are without wealth may, at some future time, become prosperous; those who are destitute of kindness are utterly destitute; for them there is no change
modern: Someone who loses wealth can eventually regain it, but someone who loses grace is completely ruined and can never recover.

old: If you consider, the virtue of him who is without kindness is like the perception of the true being by him who is without wisdom
modern: The good deeds of someone without kindness are like the true meaning of a text being understood by someone without wisdom.

old: When a man is about to rush upon those who are weaker than himself, let him remember how he has stood (trembling) before those who are stronger than himself
modern: When you are about to harm someone weaker than yourself, remember how you tremble in fear before those who are stronger than you.

old: How can he be possessed of kindness, who to increase his own flesh, eats the flesh of other creatures
modern: How can someone who eats the flesh of other creatures to increase their own flesh be considered gracious?

old: As those possess no property who do not take care of it, so those possess no kindness who feed on flesh
modern: Someone who does not protect their wealth has no use for it, just as someone who eats meat has no use for grace.

old: Like the (murderous) mind of him who carries a weapon (in his hand), the mind of him who feasts with pleasure on the body of another (creature), has no regard for goodness
modern: The mind of someone who eats the flesh of another creature is like the mind of someone who carries a weapon; it does not think of goodness or feel compassion.

old: If it be asked what is kindness and what its opposite, the answer would be preservation and destruction of life; and therefore it is not right to feed on the flesh (obtained by taking away life)
modern: Kindness means preserving life and its opposite means destroying it, so it is not right to feed on flesh obtained by taking life.

old: Not to eat flesh contributes to the continuance of life; therefore if a man eat flesh, hell will not open its mouth (to let him escape out, after he has once fallen in)
modern: Not eating flesh helps life continue, and if someone does eat it, hell will not open its mouth to let them escape.

old: If the world does not destroy life for the purpose of eating, then no one would sell flesh for the sake of money
modern: If people did not kill living beings to eat their flesh, then no one would sell meat for money.

old: If men should come to know that flesh is nothing but the unclean ulcer of a body, let them abstain from eating it
modern: If people understood that eating meat is like eating the ulcer of another living being, they would stop eating it.

old: The wise, who have freed themselves from mental delusion, will not eat the flesh which has been severed from an animal
modern: People whose minds are free from delusion do not eat meat that has been severed from a living being.

old: Not to kill and eat (the flesh of) an animal, is better than the pouring forth of ghee etc, in a thousand sacrifices
modern: It is better not to kill and eat an animal's flesh than to pour a thousand offerings of ghee into a fire for sacrifices.

old: All creatures will join their hands together, and worship him who has never taken away life, nor eaten flesh
modern: All living beings will join their hands in reverence to someone who does not kill any creature and refuses to eat meat.

old: The nature of religious discipline consists, in the endurance (by the ascetic) of the sufferings which it brings on himself, and in abstaining from giving pain to others
modern: True penance means enduring the hardships that come your way without causing pain to other living beings.

old: Austerities can only be borne, and their benefits enjoyed, by those who have practised them (in a former birth); it will be useless for those who have not done so, to attempt to practise them (now)
modern: Austerities and spiritual discipline are only truly beneficial for those who have already practiced them in a previous life, so attempting them without that prior foundation is a useless effort.

old: It is to provide food etc, for the ascetics who have abandoned (the desire of earthly possessions) that other persons have forgotten (to practise) austerity ?
modern: Have other people forgotten to practice austerity in order to provide for the needs of ascetics?

old: If (the ascetic) desire the destruction of his enemies, or the aggrandizement of his friends, it will be effected by (the power of) his austerities
modern: Through the power of their austerities, someone can destroy their enemies and elevate their friends if they set their minds to it.

old: Religious dislipline is practised in this world, because it secures the attainment of whatever one may wish to enjoy (in the world to come)
modern: People practise austerity in this world because it secures whatever they may wish to enjoy in the world to come.

old: Those discharge their duty who perform austerities; all others accomplish their own destruction, through the entanglement of the desire (of riches and sensual pleasure)
modern: Those who perform austerities are the ones who do their duty, while others, entangled in desire, engage in futile actions.

old: Just as gold is purified as heated in the fire, will those shine, who have endured the burning of pain (in frequent austerities)
modern: Just as gold is purified when it is heated in fire, those who have endured the burning of austerity will shine.

old: All other creatures will worship him who has attained the control of his own soul
modern: Every other creature will worship someone who has gained control of their own soul.

old: Those who have attained the power which religious discipline confers, will be able also to pass the limit of Yama, (the God of death)
modern: Those who gain power through religious discipline can even conquer death.

old: Because there are few who practise austerity and many who do not, there are many destitute and few rich in this world
modern: Because there are few people who practice austerity and many who do not, many people in the world are poor while few are rich.

old: The five elements (of his body) will laugh within him at the feigned conduct of the deceitful minded man
modern: The five elements of the body laugh inside a deceitful person at their pretended conduct.

old: What avails an appearance (of sanctity) high as heaven, if his mind suffers (the indulgence) of conscious sin
modern: What good is a reputation for being very holy if your own conscience knows you have done wrong?

old: The assumed appearance of power, by a man who has no power (to restrain his senses and perform austerity), is like a cow feeding on grass covered with a tiger's skin
modern: Pretending to be a powerful ascetic while lacking the self-control to master one's mind is like a cow wearing a tiger's skin to graze on the crops.

old: He who hides himself under the mask of an ascetic and commits sins, like a sportsman who conceals himself in the thicket to catch birds
modern: Pretending to be a holy person while doing evil deeds is like a hunter hiding in the bushes to catch birds.

old: The false conduct of those who say they have renounced all desire will one day bring them sorrows that will make them cry out, "Oh! what have we done, what have we done."
modern: Those who pretend to be free from attachment but secretly act wrongly will later suffer many sorrows and cry out, "What have we done.

old: Amongst living men there are none so hard-hearted as those who without to saking (desire) in their heart, falsely take the appearance of those who have forsaken (it)
modern: There is no one more cruel than a person who lives by cheating others while pretending to be a saint, even though they have not truly given up their inner desires.

old: (The world) contains persons whose outside appears (as fair) as the (red) berry of the Abrus, but whose inside is as black as the nose of that berry
modern: Some people in the world look as bright red as the outside of the kunri berry, but their minds are as black as the inside of its nose.

old: There are many men of masked conduct, who perform their ablutions, and (make a show) of
modern: Many people whose minds are impure bathe in water and make an outward show of purity.

old: As, in its use, the arrow is crooked, and the curved lute is straight, so by their deeds, (and not by their appearance) let (the uprightness or crookedness of) men be estimated
modern: The straight arrow acts cruelly and the curved lute sounds sweet, so judge people by their deeds and not by their appearance.

old: There is no need of a shaven crown, nor of tangled hair, if a man abstain from those deeds which the wise have condemned
modern: There is no point in shaving your head or growing your hair long if you stop doing the things that people condemn.

old: Let him, who desires not to be despised, keep his mind from (the desire of) defrauding another of the smallest thing
modern: Someone who wants to live without being despised by others should protect their mind from even the thought of stealing or cheating others out of any possession.

old: Even the thought (of sin) is sin; think not then of crafiily stealing the property of another
modern: Even the thought is a sin, so do not think of cunningly taking what belongs to another.

old: The property, which is acquired by fraud, will entirely perish, even while it seems to increase
modern: Wealth gained by fraud will perish entirely, even while it seems to be growing.

old: The eager desire of defrauding others will, when it brings forth its fruit, produce undying sorrow
modern: A strong desire to cheat others out of their wealth will, when it bears fruit, cause undying sorrow.

old: The study of kindness and the exercise of benevolence is not with those who watch for another's forgetfulness, though desire of his property
modern: Kindness and generosity are not found in those who watch for another's lapse out of desire for their property.

old: They cannot walk steadfastly, according to rule, who eagerly desire to defraud others
modern: People who are intensely greedy to steal others' wealth cannot live a life of moderation and restraint.

old: That black-knowledge which is called fraud, is not in those who desire that greatness which is called rectitude
modern: People who desire to live with measured wisdom do not have the dark knowledge of fraud.

old: Deceit dwells in the mind of those who are conversant with fraud, even as virtue in the minds of those who are conversant with rectitude
modern: Virtue resides in the hearts of those who understand righteousness, while deceit resides in the hearts of those who understand fraud.

old: Those, who are acquainted with nothing but fraud, will perish in the very commission of transgression
modern: Those who know nothing but theft will perish while committing their crimes.

old: Even their body will fail the fraudulent; but even the world of the gods will not fail those who are free from fraud
modern: Even their own body fails those who cheat, while even the world of the gods does not fail those who are free from fraud.

old: Truth is the speaking of such words as are free from the least degree of evil (to others)
modern: Truth is speaking words that do not cause any harm to anyone.

old: Even falsehood has the nature of truth, if it confer a benefit that is free from fault
modern: Even falsehood can be considered truth if it brings a faultless benefit to others.

old: Let not a man knowingly tell a lie; for after he has told the lie, his mind will burn him (with the memory of his guilt)
modern: A person should not lie about something that their own heart knows is true, because once the lie is told, their own mind will punish them with guilt and sorrow.

old: He who, in his conduct, preserves a mind free from deceit, will dwell in the minds of all men
modern: Someone who lives without any deceit in their heart will dwell in the hearts of all people.

old: He, who speaks truth with all his heart, is superior to those who make gifts and practise austerities
modern: Speaking the truth sincerely from the heart is better than giving gifts and practicing austerities.

old: There is no praise like the praise of never uttering a falsehood: without causing any suffering, it will lead to every virtue
modern: There is no praise like the praise of never lying, and this truthfulness itself gives all virtues without the person even realizing it.

old: If a man has the power to abstain from falsehood, it will be well with him, even though he practise no other virtue
modern: If someone has the power to keep from lying, it will go well with them even if they practise no other virtue.

old: Purity of body is produced by water and purity of mind by truthfulness
modern: Water makes the body pure, and truth makes the mind pure.

old: All lamps of nature are not lamps; the lamp of truth is the lamp of the wise
modern: Not every lamp is truly a lamp; the lamp of truth is the lamp of the wise.

old: Amidst all that we have seen (described) as real (excellence), there is nothing so good as truthfulness
modern: Among all the good things we have seen in the scriptures, there is nothing better than truthfulness.

old: He restrains his anger who restrains it when it can injure; when it cannot injure, what does it matter whether he restrain it, or not ?
modern: Someone truly restrains anger when they hold it back where it could injure; where it cannot injure, it hardly matters whether they restrain it or not.

old: Anger is bad, even when it cannot injure; when it can injure; there is no greater evil
modern: Being angry at people who have no power to hurt you is harmful to yourself, but being angry at people who actually have the power to hurt you is an even worse evil.

old: Forget anger towards every one, as fountains of evil spring from it
modern: You should forget the anger you feel towards anyone, because anger is the source of all evil.

old: Is there a greater enemy than anger, which kills both laughter and joy ?.
modern: Anger is a greater enemy than any other foe because it kills both the smile on the face and the joy in the heart.

old: If a man would guard himself, let him guard against anger; if he do not guard it, anger will kill him
modern: To protect yourself, you must guard against anger, because if you do not, anger will destroy you.

old: The fire of anger will burn up even the pleasant raft of friendship
modern: The fire of anger will burn up even the helpful raft of friendship.

old: Destruction will come upon him who ragards anger as a good thing, as surely as the hand of him who strikes the ground will not fail
modern: Someone who treats anger as a source of strength will face ruin, just as a hand that strikes the ground cannot avoid feeling the pain.

old: Though one commit things against you as painful (to bear) as if a bundle of fire had been thrust upon you, it will be well, to refrain, if possible, from anger
modern: Even if someone causes you pain as severe as being burned by a massive fire, it is best to avoid getting angry at them if you possibly can.

old: If a man never indulges anger in his heart, he will at once obtain whatever he has thought of
modern: If a person does not think of anger in their heart, they will immediately obtain everything they have thought of.

old: Those, who give way to excessive anger, are no better than dead men; but those, who are freed from it, are equal to those who are freed (from death)
modern: Someone who has excessive anger is like a dead person, but someone who completely gives up anger is like someone who has given up everything.

old: It is the determination of the spotless not to cause sorrow to others, although they could (by so causing) obtain the wealth which confers greatness
modern: Even if they could obtain wealth that brings greatness by causing harm to others, the principle of the pure is to never cause pain to anyone.

old: It is the determination of the spotless not to do evil, even in return, to those who have cherished enmity and done them evil
modern: Someone who gets angry and harms you should not be harmed in return, because the spotless do not do evil even to those who have done them evil.

old: In an ascetic inflict suffering even on those who hate him, when he has not done them any evil, it will afterwards give him irretrievable sorrow
modern: If you retaliate and cause harm to people who hate you even though you have done them no harm, that action will bring you unavoidable and inescapable suffering.

old: The (proper) punishment to those who have done evil (to you), is to put them to shame by showing them kindness, in return and to forget both the evil and the good done on both sides
modern: The best way to punish someone who has harmed you is to do them a kindness, which will shame them, and then forget both the harm they did and any good you have done.

old: What benefit has he derived from his knowledge, who does not endeavour to keep off pain from another as much as from himself ?
modern: What benefit is there in being wise if you do not protect others from pain as you would your own?

old: Let not a man consent to do those things to another which, he knows, will cause sorrow
modern: Do not agree to do to another what you know will cause them sorrow.

old: It is the chief of all virtues not knowingly to do any person evil, even in the lowest degree, and at any time
modern: It is the highest virtue not to cause harm to anyone, even in the smallest way, at any time, or even in thought.

old: Why does a man inflict upon other creatures those sufferings, which he has found by experience are sufferings to himself ?
modern: If someone knows through their own experience how painful it is to be harmed, why would they ever harm another living being?

old: If a man inflict sorrow upon others in the morning, it will come upon him unsought in the very evening
modern: If you harm others in the morning, the same harm will come to you in the evening.

old: Sorrow will come upon those who cause pain to others; therfore those, who desire to be free from sorrow, give no pain to others
modern: Evils return to the one who causes them, so people who want to be free from sorrow will not harm others.

old: Never to destroy life is the sum of all virtuous conduct The destruction of life leads to every evil
modern: Virtue is simply not killing any living being, because killing causes every kind of evil.

old: The chief of all (the virtues) which authors have summed up, is the partaking of food that has been shared with others, and the preservation of the mainfold life of other creatures
modern: Sharing food with others and protecting all living beings is the most important virtue among all those taught in the scriptures.

old: Not to destroy life is an incomparably (great) good next to it in goodness ranks freedom from falsehood
modern: Not killing is the greatest good, and next to it is not speaking falsehood.

old: Good path is that which considers how it may avoid killing any creature
modern: The good path is the one that avoids killing any living being.

old: Of all those who, fearing the permanence of earthly births, have abandoned desire, he is the chief who, fearing (the guilt of) murder, considers how he may avoid the destruction of life
modern: Among all those who renounce worldly life out of a fear of the cycle of birth and death, the greatest is the one who fears the sin of murder and strictly avoids killing.

old: Yama, the destroyer of life, will not attack the life of him, who acts under the determination of never destroying life
modern: Death, which devours life, will not attack the life of someone who has resolved never to destroy life.

old: Let no one do that which would destroy the life of another, although he should by so doing, lose his own life
modern: Even if you must lose your own life, you should not kill another person to save yourself.

old: The advantage which might flow from destroying life in sacrifice, is dishonourable to the wise (who renounced the world), even although it should be said to be productive of great good
modern: Even if killing in a sacrifice brings great gain, the wise consider the gain from killing to be dishonorable.

old: Men who destroy life are base men, in the estimation of those who know the nature of meanness.
modern: Those who live by destroying life are base people in the eyes of those who understand what meanness is.

old: (The wise) will say that men of diseased bodies, who live in degradation and in poverty, are those who separated the life from the body of animals (in a former birth)
modern: Wise people say that those who suffer from poverty and disease while living a miserable life are people who killed animals in their past lives by taking their lives away from their bodies.

old: That ignorance which considers those things to be stable which are not so, is dishonourable (to the wise)
modern: Thinking that impermanent things are permanent is a foolish and degrading state of mind.
