old: I say I would be firm, but alas, my malady breaks out from its concealment and appears in public
modern: I used to think I was full of self-control, but my hidden desire has broken through my concealment and been exposed in public.

old: The dignity that would not go after an absent lover is not known to those who are sticken by love
modern: The dignity that does not pursue someone who has left you is something that someone who is in love cannot understand.

old: The sorrow I have endured by desiring to go after my absent lover, in what way is it excellent?
modern: What kind of sorrow is this love sickness that makes me want to follow my lover who has left me, and how is it excellent?

old: I know nothing like shame when my beloved does from love (just) what is desired (by me)
modern: When the person I love does what I desire out of love, I forget all shame.

old: Are not the enticing words of my trick-abounding roguish lover the weapon that breaks away my feminine firmness?
modern: The sweet, humble words of a deceitful lover who is an expert in many tricks are the weapon that breaks a woman's resolve.

old: I said I would feign dislike and so went (away); (but) I embraced him the moment I say my mind began to unite with him!
modern: I went away pretending to be angry, but when I saw my heart starting to unite with him, I embraced him.

old: Is it possible for those whose hearts melt like fat in the fire to say they can feign a strong dislike and remain so?
modern: Can people whose hearts melt like fat in the fire really say they will stand aloof and feign a quarrel after being together?

old: My finger has worn away by marking (on the wall) the days he has been absent while my eyes have lost their lustre and begin to fail
modern: My eyes have lost their brightness from watching for his return, and my fingers have worn down from counting the days he has been gone.

old: O you bright-jewelled maid, if I forget (him) today, my shoulders will lose their beauty even in the other life and make my bracelets loose
modern: If I forget my lover today, my shoulders will lose their beauty and my bracelets will slip off.

old: I still live by longing for the arrival of him who has gone out of love for victory and with valour as his guide
modern: A lover who went abroad seeking victory with his enthusiasm as his only companion, left me because he did not want to enjoy happiness with me or have me as a companion. I am still alive only because I long to see him return and reject those other pursuits.

old: My heart is rid of its sorrow and swells with rapture to think of my absent lover returning with his love
modern: My heart is filled with rapture and climbs up the branches of a tree to look for my lover who left me, as I think of him returning with his love.

old: May I look on my lover till I am satisfied and thereafter will vanish the sallowness of my slender shoulders
modern: I just want to gaze at my husband until I am completely satisfied, and then the pallor on my slender shoulders will naturally fade away.

old: May my husband return some day; and then will I enjoy (him) so as to destroy all this agonizing sorrow
modern: My lover should come to me one day, and when he does, I will fully enjoy him so that all my agonizing sorrow is destroyed.

old: On the return of him who is as dear as my eyes, am I displeased or am I to embrace (him); or am I to do both?
modern: When my beloved returns, should I sulk at him for delaying his arrival, or should I cry from my own helplessness, or should I do both?

old: Let the king fight and gain (victories); (but) let me be united to my wife and feast the evening
modern: May the king fight and win, and let me be united with my wife to feast this evening.

old: To those who suffer waiting for the day of return of their distant lovers one day is as long as seven days
modern: For those who wait and yearn for the return of a distant spouse, one day feels as long as seven.

old: After (my wife) has died of a broken heart, what good will there be if she is to receive me, has received me, or has even embraced me?
modern: If a woman's heart breaks from the pain of separation and she dies, what is the use of her meeting or embracing me afterward?

old: Though you would conceal (your feelings), your painted eyes would not, for, transgressing (their bounds), they tell (me) something
modern: Even if you hide your feelings, your painted eyes refuse to stay silent and will tell me that you do not want to be separated from me.

old: Unusually great is the female simplicity of your maid whose beauty fills my eyes and whose shoulders resemble the bamboo
modern: The simple woman with beautiful eyes and bamboo-like shoulders has an abundance of feminine modesty.

old: There is something that is implied in the beauty of this woman, like the thread that is visible in a garland of gems
modern: There is a hidden meaning in a woman's beauty, like the thread that is visible inside a string of jewels.

old: There is something in the unmatured smile of this maid like the fragrance that is contained in an unblossomed bud
modern: A young woman's budding smile hides a secret, much like a fragrance concealed inside an unbloomed bud.

old: The well-meant departure of her whose bangles are tight-fitting contains a remedy that can cure my great sorrow
modern: The secret signal my wife sent me when she left, hiding it from everyone else, holds the cure for my deep sorrow. Her playful glance, while wearing her tight bangles, also contains the medicine to heal my pain.

old: The embrace that fills me with comfort and gladness is capable of enduring (my former) sorrow and meditating on his want of love
modern: His loving embrace comforts me, but it also makes me realize he will soon leave me and no longer love me.

old: My bracelets have understood before me the (mental) separation of him who rules the cool seashore
modern: My armlets knew about my lover's mental separation from me before I did. They fell off because they sensed his heart was no longer with me, even though his body was still here.

old: It was but yesterday my lover departed (from me); and it is seven days since my complexion turned sallow
modern: My lover left me yesterday, and it has been seven days since my body turned sallow.

old: She looked at her bracelets, her tender shoulders, and her feet; this was what she did there (significantly)
modern: She looked at her armlets, her tender shoulders, and her feet, and this was her way of telling him to come with her.

old: To express their love-sickness by their eyes and resort to begging bespeaks more than ordinary female excellence
modern: Expressing love-sickness through the eyes and praying for relief is an even more feminine trait than a woman's natural womanhood.

old: To please by thought and cheer by sight is peculiar, not to liquor but lust
modern: The joy felt when thinking of someone and the happiness seen when looking at them belong to love, not to wine.

old: If women have a lust that exceeds even the measure of the palmyra fruit, they will not desire (to feign) dislike even as much as the millet
modern: When a woman's desire grows as large as a palmyra fruit, she should not sulk with her lover even as much as a millet grain.

old: Though my eyes disregard me and do what is pleasing to my husband, still will they not be satisfied unless they see him
modern: Even if he slighted me and did only what he wanted, my eyes would not be at peace without seeing him.

old: O my friend! I was prepared to feign displeasure but my mind forgetting it was ready to embrace him.
modern: My friend, I went to see him ready to pretend to be angry, but my heart forgot my plan and was eager to embrace him.

old: Like the eyes which see not the pencil that paints it, I cannot see my husband's fault (just) when I meet him
modern: When I am close to my husband, I cannot see his faults, just like eyes that fail to see the kohl stick that paints them. Even though I had been thinking about his past mistakes when we were apart, seeing him in person makes me forget them entirely.

old: When I see my husband, I do not see any faults; but when I do not see him, I do not see anything but faults
modern: When I see my husband, I do not see any of his faults, and when I do not see him, I do not see anything except his faults.

old: Like those who leap into a stream which they know will carry them off, why should a wife feign dislike which she knows cannot hold out long?
modern: Why should a wife feign anger and quarrel with her husband, knowing that her anger will not last long, just as someone jumps into a stream knowing it will sweep them away?

old: O you rogue! your breast is to me what liquor is to those who rejoice in it, though it only gives them an unpleasant disgrace
modern: Your breast is like wine to drunkards, who keep wanting it even when it brings them disgrace.

old: Sexual delight is more delicate than a flower, and few are those who understand its real nature
modern: Love is more delicate than a flower, and only a few people truly understand its nature and experience its full pleasure.

old: She once feigned dislike in her eyes, but the warmth of her embrace exceeded my own
modern: She initially showed her anger with her eyes, but she forgot the quarrel and embraced him more eagerly than he did.

old: O my soul! although you have seen how his soul stands by him, how is it you do not stand by me?
modern: Even though you see that his heart belongs entirely to him and stays by his side, why do you not stand by me and instead melt only for him?

old: O my soul! although you have known him who does not love me, still do you go to him, saying "he will not be displeased."
modern: O my heart, even though you know he does not love me, you still go to him thinking he will not get angry.

old: O my soul! do you follow him at pleasure under the belief that the ruined have no friends?
modern: Why do you follow him at your own will, leaving me, because you think the ruined have no friends?

old: O my soul! you would not first seem sulky and then enjoy (him); who then would in future consult you about such things?
modern: My heart, you will not sulk first and then enjoy him; who will then consult you about such things?

old: My soul fears when it is without him; it also fears when it is with him; it is subject to incessant sorrow
modern: The heart fears being without a lover, and it also fears losing the lover once they are gained, which causes endless sorrow.

old: My mind has been (here) in order to eat me up (as it were) whenever I think of him in my solitude
modern: My heart feels like it is eating me when I think of my lover's cruelty while I am alone.

old: I have even forgotten my modesty, having been caught in my foolish mind which is not dignified enough to forget him
modern: I have forgotten my shame because my worthless, foolish mind cannot forget him.

old: My soul which clings to life thinks only of his (own) gain in the belief that it would be disgraceful for it to despise him
modern: My heart, which loves him deeply, thinks only of his greatness and refuses to despise him, because it fears that doing so would bring disgrace upon itself.

old: Who would help me out of one's distress, when one's own soul refuses help to one?
modern: If someone's own heart does not help them when they are in pain, who else will support them?

old: It is hardly possible for strangers to behave like relations, when one's own soul acts like a stranger
modern: It is easy for strangers to be unfriendly when one's own heart is not one's own.

old: Let us witness awhile his keen suffering; just feign dislike and embrace him not
modern: Feign sulk and do not embrace him so that we can watch his distress for a little while.

old: A little dislike is like salt in proportion; to prolong it a little is like salt a little too much
modern: A little bit of sulking adds spice to love, but keeping it up too long makes it bitter, just like too much salt ruins a dish.

old: For men not to embrace those who have feigned dislike is like torturing those already in agony
modern: Leaving someone who is sulking without an embrace is like adding to the pain of someone who is already suffering.

old: Not to reconcile those who have feigned dislike is like cutting a faded creeper at its root
modern: Not comforting a partner who is upset and pouting is like cutting a dried-up vine right at the root.

old: An increased shyness in those whose eyes are like flowers is beautiful even to good and virtuous husbands
modern: Even good and virtuous men find the pouting of wives with flower-like eyes to be a lovely grace.

old: Sexual pleasure, without prolonged and short-lived dislike, is like too ripe, and unripe fruit
modern: Love without any conflict, whether big or small, is like a fruit that is either too ripe or too unripe.

old: The doubt as to whether intercourse would take place soon or not, creates a sorrow (even) in feigned dislike
modern: A lover's quarrel causes pain because they worry the happy reunion will be delayed.

old: What avails sorrow when I am without a wife who can understand the cause of my sorrow?
modern: What good is grieving when there is no lover to understand the cause of the sorrow?

old: Like water in the shade, dislike is delicious only in those who love
modern: Water is pleasant in the shade, and sulking is pleasant only with loved ones. Just as water is refreshing near the shade, arguments are enjoyable only with people you love.

old: It is nothing but strong desire that makes her mind unite with me who can leave her to her own dislike
modern: The heart desires to reunite with the person who left it pining and ignored its sulking. This intense desire is the sole reason for this longing.

old: You are given to prostitution; all those who are born as womankind enjoy you with their eyes in an ordinary way I will not embrace you
modern: You are a prostitute. All women look at you with desire, so I will not embrace your chest.

old: When I continued to be sulky he sneezed and thought I would (then) wish him a long life
modern: A man sneezed while his lover was sulking, hoping she would finally speak to him and wish him a long life.

old: Even if I were adorned with a garland of branch-flowers, she would say I did so to show it to another woman
modern: Even if I wear a garland of branch-flowers, she will angrily accuse me of wearing it to show off to another woman.

old: When I said I loved her more than any other woman, she said "more than others, yes, more than others," and remained sulky
modern: When I said I loved her more than anyone else, she sulked and asked, "More than whom, more than whom?

old: When I said I would never part from her in this life her eyes were filled with tears
modern: I told my lover I would never leave her in this life, and she cried, thinking we would have to part in the next one.

old: When I said I had remembered her, she said I had forgotten her and relaxing her embrace, began to feign dislike
modern: I told my lover that I had been thinking of her, and she started crying and pretending to be upset because she thought I had forgotten her.

old: When I sneezed she blessed me, but at once changed (her mind) and wept, asking, "At the thought of whom did you sneeze?"
modern: When I sneezed, she first blessed me but then immediately became angry and cried, asking who I was thinking of when I sneezed.

old: When I suppressed my sneezing, she wept saying, "I suppose you (did so) to hide from me your own people's remembrance of you"
modern: When I suppressed a sneeze, she cried that I was hiding from her the thoughts of my own people.

old: 'I see', quoth she, 'to other folks How you are wondrous kind' Even when I try to remove her dislike, she is displeased and says, "This is the way you behave
modern: Even when I try to soothe her and apologize for my mistakes, she gets angry and accuses me of behaving the exact same way with other women.

old: Even when I look on her contemplating (her beauty), she is displeased and says, "With whose thought have you (thus) looked on my person?"
modern: Even when I silently think about and gaze at her incomparable beauty, she gets angry and asks, "Who are you thinking of and comparing me to?

old: Although my husband is free from defects, the way in which he embraces me is such as to make me feign dislike
modern: Although he has no faults, pretending to be upset makes him love me more.

old: His love will increase though it may (at first seem to) fade through the short-lived distress caused by (my) dislike
modern: The small pain caused by a lover's quarrel makes the great love they show afterward even more valuable, even if it seems to have faded a little.

old: Is there a celestial land that can please like the feigned dislike of those whose union resembles that of earth and water?
modern: Is there a heaven more blissful than the feigned dislike between lovers whose hearts are as united as earth and water?

old: In prolonged dislike after an embrace there is a weapon that can break my heart
modern: In a lingering embrace where a lover refuses to let go, there is a weapon that breaks my heart. This weapon represents the feigned anger and sweet words of affection used to keep the couple together, which ultimately destroy my resolve.

old: Though free from defects, men feel pleased when they cannot embrace the delicate shoulders of those whom they love
modern: Even if someone is without fault, there is a special pleasure in being estranged from the delicate shoulders of the woman he loves.

old: To digest what has been eaten is more delightful than to eat more; likewise love is more delightful in dislike than intercourse
modern: It is sweeter to digest a meal than to eat it, and it is sweeter to quarrel in love than to be united.

old: Those are conquerors whose dislike has been defeated and that is proved by the love (which
modern: The one who yields in a lovers' quarrel is the true winner, and this is proven when they reunite.

old: Will I enjoy once more through her dislike, the pleasure of that love that makes her forehead perspire?
modern: Will we get to enjoy the sweetness of making love again, which causes her forehead to sweat, if we have another playful quarrel?

old: May the bright-jewelled one feign dislike, and may the night be prolonged for me to implore her!
modern: May the woman with shining jewels continue to sulk, and may the night be prolonged so I can keep pleading with her.

old: Dislike adds delight to love; and a hearty embrace (thereafter) will add delight to dislike
modern: Feigned dislike adds spice to love, and the pleasure grows when they finally unite.
